faq.title: FAQ
faq.label: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: Choosing a studio is an expensive decision to undo. Below are the questions people ask us before signing, answered the way we'd answer them on a call.

price.question: What does a project cost?
price.answer: It depends on scope, and you get the number on the first call. A full identity isn't a landing page. We work to a fixed project price: you know what it costs before we start, not after.

time.question: How long does it take?
time.answer: A site, four to eight weeks. An identity, six to ten. The variable is rarely us: it's how long content takes to arrive and answers take to come back.

remote.question: Do you work with brands outside Mexico?
remote.answer: Yes, and most of it ships remotely. From Mexico City the day overlaps with all of the Americas and reaches the European morning.

ownership.question: Who owns what you make?
ownership.answer: You do. When the project closes you get the editable files and the accounts, with no licences that expire and nothing left sitting on a server of ours.

scope.question: Can I hire just one part?
scope.answer: Yes, knowing what you give up: the site, the campaign and the motion are designed together so they say the same thing. Separately it works; together it works better.

start.question: What do you need from me to start?
start.answer: Half an hour to understand the business, someone who can say yes or no without asking four people, and whatever you already have — even if it's a logo inside a PDF.

branding.title: Branding and design
branding.description: Identity, naming and visual systems for brands that need to look like what they already are.

process.title: What an identity includes
process.intro: Four phases, each one ending with something you receive. A full identity takes six to ten weeks.

diagnosis.title: Diagnosis
diagnosis.text: We talk to whoever runs the business and look at how your brand reads today next to its competitors.
diagnosis.deliverable: Brief signed by both of us

strategy.title: Strategy
strategy.text: What the brand promises, who it speaks to and in what voice. If it needs a name, this is where we decide it.

identity.title: Identity
identity.text: Logo, type, color and the rules that hold them together. You review it on real pieces, not on loose boards.

rollout.title: Applications
rollout.text: Packaging, stationery, signage or social: whatever your brand needs to go out into the world.

faq.intro: What people ask us before starting an identity.

price.question: How much does an identity cost?
price.answer: It depends on what it includes: a logo with its guidelines doesn't cost the same as a system with naming, packaging and signage. We work with a fixed budget, so you know the number before we start.

naming.question: Do you do naming too?
naming.answer: Yes, when the brand needs it. It happens in the strategy phase, before design, because the name changes what the logo has to solve.

rebrand.question: Can you evolve a brand that already exists?
rebrand.answer: Yes, and it's a good part of what we do. First we look at what your people already recognize so we don't throw it away, and then we decide what changes.

ownership.question: Who owns the files?
ownership.answer: You do. At the end we hand over the editable files, the licensed typefaces and the guidelines, with nothing that depends on us.

cta.title: Tell us about your brand and let's see where to start.

motion.title: Motion
motion.description: Brand animation, video and interface motion, made by the same team that designs the identity.

process.title: From idea to final piece
process.intro: Each phase is approved before the next one starts, so changes come while they are still cheap.

script.title: Script
script.text: We decide what has to happen in the first few seconds and what the viewer takes away.

storyboard.title: Storyboard
storyboard.text: Frame by frame, before animating anything. This is when changing something costs little.

animation.title: Animation
animation.text: Movement, rhythm and sound on top of the style you already approved.

delivery.title: Delivery
delivery.text: We export each piece in the format and size of the channel where it will live.

faq.intro: What is worth knowing before ordering an animated piece.

price.question: How much does a piece cost?
price.answer: Three things drive it: how long it runs, how complex the style is and how many formats it ships in. With the script in hand we give you a fixed budget.

time.question: How long does it take?
time.answer: It depends on length and style. The delivery date is agreed before we start, together with the script.

what.question: What kind of pieces do you make?
what.answer: Animated logos, the motion of an identity, social pieces, event video and interface animation for sites and products.

brand.question: Can you work on a brand you didn't design?
brand.answer: Yes. We start from your guidelines and, if something is missing, we define how the brand moves before animating the first piece.

cta.title: Tell us what piece you need and when.

marketing.title: Marketing
marketing.description: Campaigns, content and paid media designed by the same team that makes the brand.

process.title: How we build a strategy
process.intro: Before proposing channels we look at what already works for you. Each phase leaves a document you can read without us.

diagnosis.title: Diagnosis
diagnosis.text: We review your channels, your content and the numbers you already have.

plan.title: Plan
plan.text: Which channels, with what message and what budget. No fixed packages: the plan comes from your business.

execution.title: Execution
execution.text: Campaigns, content and paid media made by the people who design the brand, so everything says the same thing.

measurement.title: Measurement
measurement.text: We read the numbers with you and adjust what isn't working.

faq.intro: What people ask us before taking a brand into channels.

price.question: How much does it cost?
price.answer: It depends on the channels and the media budget, which is kept separate from our fees so you know what pays for what. The number comes out of the diagnosis.

results.question: When do results show?
results.answer: It depends on the channel: paid media gives signals early and content takes longer to build up. The plan tells you what to expect from each one and when to review it.

accounts.question: Who owns the accounts?
accounts.answer: You do. Ad, social and analytics accounts are in your company's name; we get access.

brand.question: Do I need the brand done first?
brand.answer: No, but it helps. If the brand isn't clear yet, we start there, because a campaign can't fix a brand that doesn't know what to say.

cta.title: Tell us where your brand is today and where you want to take it.
cta.titleHighlight: where you want to take it

web.title: Web development
web.description: Custom sites that are fast and editable, designed and built by the same team.

process.title: How we make a site
process.intro: Design and code in the same team, so what you approve on screen is what gets published. A site takes four to eight weeks.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.text: Which pages, what content and what visitors need to be able to do.

design.title: Design
design.text: Desktop and mobile screens, reviewed with you before writing a line of code.

build.title: Development
build.text: We build it on a content management system so your team can change text and images without asking us.

launch.title: Launch
launch.text: We publish, check speed, search and accessibility, and show you how to use the CMS.

faq.intro: What is worth knowing before rebuilding a site.

price.question: How much does a site cost?
price.answer: It depends on how many pages, how many languages and what it has to connect to, like a store or a CRM. With the sitemap we give you a fixed budget.

time.question: How long does it take?
time.answer: Four to eight weeks. What moves it most is when the content arrives: copy, photos and decisions.

edit.question: Will I be able to edit it?
edit.answer: Yes. Everything that changes often, like copy, images or projects, is edited from a CMS, without touching code.

ownership.question: Who owns the site?
ownership.answer: You do: the code, the domain and the access are in your company's name.

cta.title: Tell us what site you need and when.
